holidays.name: Dewey Decimal System Day
holidays.description: A day for book lovers to tip their hats to the number system that keeps library shelves in order. Wander the stacks, find a favorite section, or sort your own bookshelf by decimal. You could also finally find that one book you've been hunting for.
holidays.origin: The day honors Melvil Dewey, the librarian who created the Dewey Decimal Classification in the 1870s. He sorted knowledge into ten main classes, and the system took over libraries around the world.
holidays.funFact: Melvil Dewey tried to simplify his own name by dropping the extra letters in his first name, and he spelled it 'Dui' for a while. Today the Dewey system is used in libraries in well over 100 countries.

holidays.name: Festival for the Souls of Dead Whales
holidays.description: A solemn and unusual observance that honors whales that have died. It invites people to reflect on the lives of these giants of the sea and on the oceans they travel.
holidays.origin: The festival comes from Japanese whaling-community tradition, where memorial rites were held to comfort the spirits of whales that had been caught. It is observed on December 10 as an unofficial remembrance.
holidays.funFact: Some Japanese coastal villages built memorial mounds and kept records of the whales they caught, and the practice of remembering them goes back centuries.

holidays.name: National Lager Day
holidays.description: A day to raise a glass of crisp, cold lager, the world's most popular style of beer. Try a pilsner, a Munich helles, or an amber lager, and pair it with pretzels.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin that has become a favorite on beer lovers' calendars.
holidays.funFact: The word 'lager' comes from the German word for 'storage.' The beer gets its name from the cold cellars and caves where brewers aged it.
